16.1 INTRODUCTION
Cutting the cloth for sewing is an art in itself The entire sewing and fitting of the garment
depend upon cutting. In order to make a good dress, first a pattern is cut on which the
design is set to see the final effect. Before cutting the cloth, the different parts of the
garment are cut on paper and set aside. There are then used to conveniently cut the cloth
later on. A drafting is made according to body measurements and then the paper pattern
is made. The pattern has to be good in order to get a good fitting. One also needs to have
knowledge of the different types ofpatterns, how and where they are used, etc.

16.3 BASIC PATTERN
The drafting is made on paper and then cut to make a pattern. This paper pattern is
carefully inspected before cutting the cloth. The paper pattern is made exactly according
to the measurement and the style of the garment. This is why the paper pattern is called
the prototype of the garment. It is essential to have a correct pattern. A paper pattern is .

called a tailor's friend.
Pattern can be made in two ways -;
i)
The final pattern is made directly with the body measurements.
ii)
The final pattern is made after adjusting the design according to fashion on the
basic pattern made with the body measurements.
The pattern for ordinary clothes is made by the first method. The second method is used
for making patterns for fashionable dresses and in factories. A pattern should be carefully
put away for future use and for adapting according to fashion.
There are three ways of storing patterns -
. 1.
Individual patterns are stored in shops. The are stored by listing the customers
according to garments made or according to address. The listing may also be
done on the basis of gender - make/female and child.
2.
Every factory has its own system of storing the patterns. They may be stored
according to dress size or according to fashion. Here, too, the pattern are listed.
3.
While storingpatterns onemust know the procedure used in making it.The method
of garment construction can be selected later on.
4.
Patterns made of hardboard, plastic or fibre are stored either by hanging or kept
flat. Patterns made of flimsy paper are kept folded or rolled up.
5.
Patterns should be treated against insects/worms.
A good quality and durable paper should be used for making patterns. Cardboard, plastic
or fibre can be used for making the basic block or master pattern. The pattern should be
made according to the drafting and all the measurements should be noted on it. The pattern
should be cut along the lines only afterchecking the measurements. After cutting the pattern
should be carefully stored.
Marking of pattern
It is important to place some markings on a pattern during clothing construction. It is
important to know these markings: They are -
1.
Joint
This indicates thejoining of different parts like front to back, sleeve to body, cuff
to sleeve, collar, yoke, etc.

Small cuts in the shape of 'V' are made on the edge of the pattern and cloth. These

8.
Perforation
Any marking to be made onthe cloth, is known as style feature on the pattern.
This is indicated by making small holes called perforation marks on the pattern.
These are diamond shaped. The placement of darts, pockets, etc. is indicated in
this manner. These marks are used only on paper patterns.
Making new pattern in designs according.to the fashion is known as creative pattern or
pattern construction. For example - placing yoke on shirts, creating new styles, etc.

1.
Ordinary pattern
Any pattern cut on paper is known as ordinary pattern. When the measurements
of many people are taken and a pattern is made according to the average
measurements, the pattern is called standard pattern. Whether the pattern is made
according to average measurements or individual measurements, it is an ordinary
pattern.
2.
Individual patten!
The pattern made according to a particular individuals measurements is known as
individual pattern. The style or design are also set according to the individual's
taste.
3.
Readymade pattern
These are available only in foreign countries where big companies do not accept
small order. The women there know how to sew but not how to cut the clothes.
Hence, they make use of readymade patterns available in the market. These can
be bought in v~ous
sizes and have the measurements
and the pattern layout
depicted along with detailed instructions.
4.
Final pattern
The final pattern is the one used to cut the cloth and is error free. This pattern
shows the seam allowances, turning, etc. The final pattern is made with the help
of the basic pattern. When garments are made on a large scale in factories, the
cloth estimation is done with the help of the final pattern.
5.
Block pattern
The final pattern is usually cut on chart paper or plywood infactories
where
garments are made on as large'scale. These are durable and can easily be.stored.
6.
Trade block
When a block is made for aparticular fashionable dress with the objective oflarge
scale production, it is called a trade block.
-
7.
Block pattern layout
A layout ofthe block pattern is made on a chart paper whose width equals the
width ofthe cloth. The outlines ofthe blocks are perforated with a needle. This
chart paper is placed over the cloth which is spread flat on a.table. Then China

clayis spreadover the perforated outlines and in this way the outlines aretransferred
to the cloth. The cutter in the factory then cuts along these lines.
8.
Graded pattern
When different sizes are marked on the same pattern, it is called a graded pattern.
For example, a pattern may have sizes 32", 34", 36" marked on it. There is a
difference of2" between each size.The size to be made is selected and the marking
ofthat size are transferred to the cloth for cutting. illthis way time and effort can
be saved by marking different sizes on the same pattern.
9.
Fitting Pattern
This is generally used for cutting ready made garments. These are available in sizes
like 32", 34", 36", in the market. These are made of cardboard and can be used
for a long time.
